You’ll learn how to take part, what to expect during bidding, and how much you can earn. Whether you’re new or experienced, this guide covers what you need to know.

What Is Kenton County Tax Lien Investing?

Kenton County offers tax lien certificates to help recover unpaid property taxes. When owners miss payments, the county auctions off liens. Buyers pay the tax debt and earn interest when the lien is repaid. If unpaid, buyers can take legal steps after a set time. It’s a way to earn income with a low-risk investment backed by real estate.

Important Details

Key Takeaways

  • Kenton County offers redeemable tax lien certificates to recover unpaid property taxes, providing income potential with low risk.
  • Investors can earn a fixed 12% simple interest annually on tax lien investments, with an opportunity to purchase liens at auctions or over-the-counter.
  • Due diligence is crucial; research properties to avoid hidden issues and ensure smart investments in Kenton County.
  • The auction process includes registering, submitting property lists, and drawing lots, with a clear focus on transparency and organization.
  • Kenton County’s stable economy, affordable real estate, and accessible tax lien opportunities make it an attractive choice for investors.

Fun Facts About Kenton County

  • Kenton County has about 170,000 residents.
  • It’s home to Covington, a historic city across from Cincinnati.
  • The area was named after Simon Kenton, a frontiersman.
  • Property tax collections support roads, schools, and public safety.

Attractions and Economic Highlights

Kenton County has public parks, museums, and the Behringer-Crawford Museum. Interstate 71/75 runs through the area, linking to major cities. The airport is nearby in Boone County. Major industries include logistics, healthcare, and manufacturing. The area hosts festivals, riverfront events, and has strong community ties.

Why This County Is Ideal for Tax Lien Investors

  • High returns from 12% simple interest
  • Low-risk investment secured by property
  • Large inventory of certificates each year
  • State tax lien opportunities in a stable economy

Auction Process for Tax Lien Sales

Kenton County follows Kentucky’s process with no interest-rate bidding. Buyers register, submit lists of properties, and draw for purchasing order. The Clerk sells unpaid tax liens based on priority, then in rounds of random selection.

How the Auction Works

Here is a simple look at how the auction moves from registration to final payment.

  1. Register and Submit Your Deposit

    Start by registering with the Clerk’s Office and paying the required deposit so you are approved to take part in the sale.

  2. Turn In Your Property List

    Submit the list of properties you want before the auction. This gives the county your requested parcels for the sale process.

  3. Wait While Priority Claims Are Handled First

    The Clerk processes any priority claims before moving to the general bidder pool.

  4. Follow the Random Bid Order

    After priority claims are handled, the county draws a random order for all other bidders to set the selection sequence.

  5. Select Your Lots When Your Turn Comes

    When your turn arrives, you choose from the lots available to you through the sale process.

  6. Pay Any Remaining Balance

    After the sale, you must pay any balance still due on the properties awarded to you.

  7. Receive Any Unused Deposit Back

    If part of your deposit is not used, the Clerk refunds the unused amount within 10 days

Maximum Potential Returns and Expected Returns on Kenton County Tax Lien Certificates

Investors can earn up to 12 percent simple interest annually. That means $120 on a $1,000 lien if redeemed after a year. Earnings depend on how fast the property owner pays. Some repay within months. Others take the full year. The rate is fixed, so buyers know the return upfront. Real estate backs each lien, adding safety.

Open to All Investors / Foreign Investor Participation

Kentucky welcomes both local and international investors. You don’t have to live in the state or even in the U.S. to buy liens. Investors from other countries can register by mail and follow the same rules. This opens the door to global investment opportunities. International buyers often focus on lower-cost areas like Kenton County.

Importance of Due Diligence in Kenton County Tax Lien Investing

What Due Diligence Entails

Investors must research each property. Use county records to check location, size, and value. Visit if you can. Look at tax history and confirm that there are no major legal issues. Title searches are useful. All this helps avoid problems later.

Risks of Skipping Due Diligence

Skipping your research can cost you. You may buy a lien on a burned building or landlocked lot. Some properties have hidden liens or code violations. Always do your homework before bidding. Research protects your money and increases your chances of success.

Buying Over-the-Counter (OTC) Liens/Deeds in Kenton County

How to Purchase OTC Liens/Deeds

If a lien doesn’t sell at auction, you can buy it over the counter. Visit the Kenton County Clerk’s office. Register like normal and pay the fee. Then request a list of available liens and purchase in person. You pay the amount owed plus fees.

Benefits of OTC Purchases

You don’t compete with other buyers. Interest rate is still 12 percent. It’s first-come, first-served. You can take your time and research.

Why Kenton County Is a Top Choice for Tax Lien Investors

Economic and Tax Advantages

Kenton County benefits from a solid job market and regional economy. It borders Cincinnati and has easy access to shipping and travel. Tax rules are clear. The fixed interest rate keeps risks low. Location and legal stability make it a strong place to invest.

Real Estate Market Overview

Home prices in Kenton County are affordable. There’s steady demand for housing. Vacant land and older homes offer chances to buy low. Investors can benefit from growth as the area attracts new residents and businesses.

Conclusion

Kenton County offers real value for tax lien investors. The 12 percent return, strong legal protections, and reliable process make it a great pick. The Clerk’s Office runs a clean, well-documented sale. Certificates are backed by real property, adding safety. Whether buying at auction or over the counter, investors can profit while helping the county recover taxes.

Smart investing starts with solid research. Know the rules. Review the lists. Check the properties. The time you spend upfront will protect your money and improve your returns.

Pro Tips

  • Register early and confirm all forms are complete
  • Focus on land and properties with clean title history
  • Use maps and online tools to check property size and access
  • Build a list of backup properties in case your first picks sell
  • Check leftover liens after the sale for OTC chances

FAQs

Can I fix or renovate a property after buying the lien?

No. You only own the lien, not the property. You can act after foreclosure.

How do I get full ownership if no one redeems?

Wait one year. Then file a foreclosure suit in court to take the deed.

Are other liens still owed after I buy a tax lien?

Yes. IRS liens or city code violations may still exist. Do your research first.

Can I sell my lien to someone else?

Yes. You can assign it to another buyer. Check with the Clerk for rules.

Do banks or lenders offer financing for lien purchases?

Usually not. Most investors use their own cash. These are short-term investments.
